title: Simple public-goods causes (no bridging)
description: Signable independent planks for OSS and local food: outcome wants, earmark grain (kind + place), geographic parents. Copied from statement-generation-exercises/01-simple-causes.json after Adam accepted the texts (2026-08-27). Not a complete catalog of variation. No triples.
notes: Want the outcome; do not classify it as a public good. Do not plank payroll.
Earmark grain is a ladder on more than one axis (kind of software / kind of food system / place).

Tiny seed still aligns Riverside Community Garden to fundable-projects/local-community/local-food-systems (explorer slogan). These planks are additional signable wants, not a silent replacement of that CID.

groups.title: Open-source software as a public good
notes: General plank plus specific earmarks. No parent/child implication designed yet (a Linux want need not imply the generic OSS want unless we later check that).
Vendor-capture stays as a general governance want, not payroll.

statements.text: I want widely used open-source libraries to stay maintained, documented, and patched for security problems.
notes: Adam: fine for (a) general OSS support, (b) generic advocacy, (c) earmarked delegation to someone who follows many OSS projects.

statements.text: I want Linux to stay maintained and usable as general-purpose open-source infrastructure.
I want Linux desktop software to stay maintained and usable as a daily-driver operating system.
I want open-source large language models and the tooling around them to stay available to run and improve.
I want Ethereum's open-source protocol and client software to stay maintained.
I want open-source infrastructure for Ethereum-based games to stay maintained and usable.
I do not want critical maintenance of a widely used open-source project to depend on a single vendor that can capture control of the project.

groups.title: Local food systems (signable planks, not explorer slogans)
notes: Mechanism grain (gardens, markets, CSA, farms, shorter chains) is the food analog of 'kind of software'. Place grain is often the useful earmark: CSA in Grey County, Ontario.
Geographic parents: Ontario CSA / Ontario farmers' markets are location containers so county projects roll up onto those boards (inbound implication). Not an any-combinator over counties.
implicationNotes: Designed yes: csa-grey-county-ontario → csa-ontario (narrower geography); csa-grey-county-ontario → community-supported-agriculture (conjunction → topical parent); csa-ontario → community-supported-agriculture; farmers-markets-grey-county-ontario → farmers-markets-ontario; farmers-markets-grey-county-ontario → farmers-markets; farmers-markets-ontario → farmers-markets.

Designed no: csa-ontario → csa-grey-county-ontario; community-supported-agriculture → csa-ontario; community-supported-agriculture → csa-grey-county-ontario; farmers-markets-ontario → farmers-markets-grey-county-ontario. Canada CSA would need its own direct Grey → Canada edge (non-transitive).

statements.text: I want more neighborhood and community growing of food — home gardens, shared plots, and community gardens.

notes: Topical parent for place-specific farmers' market wants. The longer 'connect local growers' mechanism is a sibling unique, not this parent — Grey cannot imply extra mechanism.

statements.text: I want more farmers' markets that connect local growers directly with nearby buyers.
I want farmers' markets in Ontario.
notes: WORKAROUND, not the nestable protocol: dropped 'more' after live attester flipped on 'I want more farmers' markets in Ontario'. Geographic containment vs attester is still Ask — see statement-generation.md Open section. Do not copy this as the parent template.

statements.text: I want more community-supported agriculture, where residents subscribe to shares from nearby farms.
I want more community-supported agriculture in Ontario.
notes: Location container. Board for this statement should show projects aligned with any nested place (e.g. Grey County) once those children imply this parent.

statements.text: I want more community-supported agriculture in Grey County, Ontario.
I want more farmers' markets in Grey County, Ontario.
I want working local farms to stay viable near where people live.
I want more of what people eat to come from nearby producers rather than through long-distance distribution alone.
